video_title: They Told Teresa Weatherspoon She'd Be a Ditch Digger. She Went and Won Olympic Gold Instead

quotes.speaker: Teresa Weatherspoon
quotes.summary_phrase: Teresa Weatherspoon on the importance of building relationships with players
quotes.excerpt: If you see someone who's gone through a little bit of what you've gone through, reel them in.
quotes.quote: If you see someone who's gone through a little bit of what you've gone through, reel them in. Hey, come here. Because you want them to know, I get it. I get it.

quotes.speaker: Teresa Weatherspoon
quotes.summary_phrase: Teresa Weatherspoon on coaching and the importance of accountability
quotes.excerpt: I can get it to you but I can't put it in the bucket.
quotes.quote: I tell you everybody was killing me at first with the passing. I can get it to you but I can't put it in the bucket. So I just kept saying, I said, you know, hey, okay, I'll take the blame. I don't have a problem with my shoulders being so broad, I'll take the blame. We didn't win that, so Cooper is killing me with that one. I was like, okay, Cooper, I said, but there's one more. There's one more. And that's the big stage. That's the GM stepping on the big stage.

quotes.speaker: Teresa Weatherspoon
quotes.summary_phrase: Teresa Weatherspoon on her father's baseball career and his influence
quotes.excerpt: My father still holds that record. When you look and see Chuck Weatherspoon, they misspelled our name.
quotes.quote: My father was a baseball player and he was well known. Growing up in the time that he was playing, of course there was the segregation and all that craziness that was happening. He played for the Minnesota Twins minor league. My dad still holds a grand slam record. My father still holds that record. When you look and see Chuck Weatherspoon, they misspelled our name, but that's my dad. When you look that up, that's my dad. His nickname is Chuck, as Charles Weatherspoon, but that's my father who still holds a grand slam record. And that was two grand slams in one game and the third one hit the fence.

quotes.speaker: Teresa Weatherspoon
quotes.summary_phrase: Teresa Weatherspoon on being told she would not be great
quotes.excerpt: No one ever thought that I would be able to get out of where I'm from.
quotes.quote: No one ever thought that I would be able to get out of where I'm from, because I would never be seen from such a small place. But so thankful for the family that I'm from. I'm from a very athletic family.

quotes.speaker: Teresa Weatherspoon
quotes.summary_phrase: Teresa Weatherspoon on a coach's belief in her potential
quotes.excerpt: She said, no. And that was the first time she had said no to something that I wanted.
quotes.quote: There was this USA uniform that she had. I never forget this. And I said, oh, I like that. I want that. She said, no. And that was the first time she had said no to something that I wanted. And she said, because you will someday have your own. I was like, no, no, no, what are you talking about? One day I'll have my own. And I'm from Pine Land and everybody's always said that I would never be able to leave here or be great.

quotes.speaker: Teresa Weatherspoon
quotes.summary_phrase: Teresa Weatherspoon on learning discipline through karate
quotes.excerpt: They put me in karate classes because my mom and dad says she needs to learn discipline now.
quotes.quote: They put me in karate classes because my mom and dad says she needs to learn discipline now. Because I wanted to win at everything and I would fight my brothers and sisters if I didn't win. I had to ask if I could play because my mom would say, no, if you play with your brothers and sisters, you have to play fair. If not, you can't play. You can't get mad if you lose and want to fight. You can't.

quotes.speaker: Teresa Weatherspoon
quotes.summary_phrase: Teresa Weatherspoon on her experience at Louisiana Tech
quotes.excerpt: That was already scary is to go into Louisiana Tech knowing the history of the program.
quotes.quote: That was already scary is to go into Louisiana Tech knowing the history of the program. They won the first NCAA championship with Kim Mulkey and Deborah Rodman and you come in and you lead them to another national championship in 1988. So what did you learn about yourself at Louisiana Tech during that experience? I wanted that challenge. I was all about challenges and everybody thought that I played with Kim Mulkey but I didn't. Kim Mulkey left and I came in and she began her coaching career and she was my coach every single day of practices and of course games. She's who I look to for leadership and guidance at the point guard position.

quotes.speaker: Teresa Weatherspoon
quotes.summary_phrase: Teresa Weatherspoon on her defensive mindset
quotes.excerpt: If you want to play on this team, you will play defense.
quotes.quote: I remember him stopping in practice and saying, if you want to play on this team, you will play defense. That's the time my mentality shifted. That was the day my mentality shifted as a freshman and I started to look around as who can I defend for him to see me that I can defend. And I went towards the best offensive player that he had at that moment. Her name was Pam Gant. They call her Pam Skeeter Gant, so that let you know she was quick as lightning, fast. I looked at her and I said, if I play defense against her, he will see me. So I started defending her every single day and that is the reason that I got an opportunity to play at Louisiana Tech as a freshman as a starter. That was my reason.

quotes.speaker: Teresa Weatherspoon
quotes.summary_phrase: Teresa Weatherspoon on the importance of being a team player
quotes.excerpt: But I'm a team player. I I I want to feel the stat sheet.
quotes.quote: But I'm a team player. I I I want to feel the stat sheet. I want to feel the stat sheet no matter what. But when that was spoken heavily to all of us, I was willing to do it. I was willing to show him that what you just said with that look he had on his face, that I can do it. I can do it and I will do it. And it was a sacrifice for the good of the team and we were all young because a lot of the players had already finished when we came in as freshmen.

quotes.speaker: Teresa Weatherspoon
quotes.summary_phrase: Teresa Weatherspoon on her mother's influence and accountability
quotes.excerpt: Did I help someone else? Did I help someone else see something differently?
quotes.quote: Every day now, when I put my head on my pillow tonight, I make sure to ask myself, did I help someone else? Did I help someone else see something differently? Did I help someone else be lifted? Did I help someone else recognize their greatness, how good they are? Did I do something good for someone else? That's important to me.

quotes.speaker: Teresa Weatherspoon
quotes.summary_phrase: Teresa Weatherspoon on the loss of her mother
quotes.excerpt: It is the ninth year of the day I lost my mom.
quotes.quote: It is the ninth year of the day I lost my mom. And it's probably been the most nine years of being lost. But when I speak about this, it makes me find that light that she was always showing me. It's the light. It's the light that you got to always find in the darkest times, in the darkest moments.

quotes.speaker: Teresa Weatherspoon
quotes.summary_phrase: Teresa Weatherspoon on the importance of being an example
quotes.excerpt: I have nieces, I have nephews, I have great nieces and nephews that I have to be an example for.
quotes.quote: I have nieces, I have nephews, I have great nieces and nephews that I have to be an example for. Even my hometown of 882 people, even those young people who just watch me, watch me move. I don't move where I have to hide anything. I move and if you watch me move, it's genuine. It's it's genuine movement and I want everyone to see that, especially my very own, that whatever you decide to do, whatever it is, it doesn't matter, because they are from Pine Land, Texas, too, that you can do it.

quotes.speaker: Teresa Weatherspoon
quotes.summary_phrase: Teresa Weatherspoon on her coaching philosophy
quotes.excerpt: I'm not going to sugarcoat it because my first question is always, what could you have done better?
quotes.quote: I'm not going to sugarcoat it because my first question is always, what could you have done better? It's always, that's my first question. And I listen. I'm going to listen. I'm not and sometimes all they want is to be heard and I'm just going to listen. I'm going to pay attention to what they're saying and then I'm then I'm then I'm going to give them my answer. And I and I will ask her, you ready for mine? You ready for mine? Okay. And we go from there.

quotes.speaker: Teresa Weatherspoon
quotes.summary_phrase: Teresa Weatherspoon on building trust with players
quotes.excerpt: I want to know the why behind what they do. And when I learn the why behind what they do, I hold them accountable to that.
quotes.quote: And my thing about players and building a relationship is I want to know your why. I want to know the why behind what they do. And when I learn the why behind what they do, I hold them accountable to that. And that's that that is an important thing is to know what their vision is. What is it that you want out of this? And and why do you want that? And how do you think you can accomplish that? That's important.

quotes.speaker: Teresa Weatherspoon
quotes.summary_phrase: Teresa Weatherspoon on the importance of constant communication
quotes.excerpt: The constant communication and conversations are constant, and that's the operative word.
quotes.quote: The constant communication and conversations are constant, and that's the operative word. Is constant communication and conversations. They're very important because the vision has to be the vision not by one person, but by all. And if that vision isn't the same, because I don't look for loyalty, I I I don't look for loyalty, I don't. I look for people who are on the same page with me as the same and with the same vision.

quotes.speaker: Teresa Weatherspoon
quotes.summary_phrase: Teresa Weatherspoon on the importance of accountability in coaching
quotes.excerpt: I'm not going to sugarcoat it because my first question is always, what could you have done better?
quotes.quote: I'm not going to sugarcoat it because my first question is always, what could you have done better? It's always, that's my first question. I'm not and sometimes all they want is to be heard and I'm just going to listen. I'm going to pay attention to what they're saying and then I'm then I'm then I'm going to give them my answer. And I and I will ask her, you ready for mine? You ready for mine? Okay. And we go from there.

quotes.speaker: Teresa Weatherspoon
quotes.summary_phrase: Teresa Weatherspoon on the importance of accountability
quotes.excerpt: Anything that you have for your young people, we all see those as expectations. Expectations.
quotes.quote: Anything that you have for your young people, we all see those as expectations. Expectations. She said, I want you to see when you're coaching your team, yes, there's expectations, but I want it to be a demand for those expectations. And that was a click on the phone, click. And I've always had that demanding approach as a player. When I go to talk to my teammates, it's a way that I would speak with them, but they knew it was a demand. I'm not I'm not just asking you, it's a demand, this is what we need. We need that. So it's more of a demanding part. No no no negotiations. We're not non-negotiables. It's a demand to get it done.

quotes.speaker: Teresa Weatherspoon
quotes.summary_phrase: Teresa Weatherspoon on finding positives in all things
quotes.excerpt: I take everything and I find positives in in all things.
quotes.quote: You take everything and I find positives in in all things. The experience really showed me who I really am because of how things happened, the way things happened. It really showed me who I really am, how strong I really am. You think you're strong until things like this happen. It really showed me just how strong I really am, but it never, not one time, not one time, did it make me not believe in who I am.

quotes.speaker: Teresa Weatherspoon
quotes.summary_phrase: Teresa Weatherspoon on her coaching philosophy and overcoming adversity
quotes.excerpt: I don't look back. I find myself and I go I move forward. I don't look back.
quotes.quote: I'm just thankful to be able to talk to you guys. I don't really talk much. I don't talk much until I get the opportunity to share with you all and I'm so willing to share what I feel, what my growth was, and the things that I've been through. I've been through some hard times, some really hard times, but I don't look back. I don't look back. I find myself and I go I move forward. I don't look back. I know that back there made me who I am to keep going. It's a bigger mirror here than to look back there.

quotes.speaker: Teresa Weatherspoon
quotes.summary_phrase: Teresa Weatherspoon praises Nneka Ogwumike's energy and impact for Seattle
quotes.excerpt: She played with such energy, confidence, and I loved every bit of it.

text_blocks.speaker: Teresa Weatherspoon
text_blocks.text: I have to give this young lady credit because of what she did coming into the game the other day for Seattle. Nneka Ogwumike. She played with such energy, confidence, and I loved every bit of it of how she came into the game. She switched that thing. She turned the energy and it never changed. They kept moving, kept rolling, and then kept going to her. Kept going to her because she was like, 'Nobody can guard me today.'

text_blocks.speaker: Allie Clifton
text_blocks.text: Yes, and Seattle got a win.

quotes.speaker: Teresa Weatherspoon
quotes.summary_phrase: Teresa Weatherspoon on the development of young WNBA talent
quotes.excerpt: It takes time to build anything. It takes time, but what I do like about that young crew
quotes.quote: It takes time to build anything. It takes time, but what I do like about that young crew is they still come in and play hard every night. They still play hard every night and I'm telling you, they score a bucket on you, you're going to know too. You're going to know they're scoring buckets. They got some young incredible talent, young incredible talent.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Robinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jordan Robinson highlights Shakira Austin's veteran leadership for the Washington Mystics
quotes.excerpt: I want to put Shakira Austin there because she is somehow the vet on this team
quotes.quote: I want to put Shakira Austin there because she is somehow the vet on this team, only five years in the league. She is surrounded by All-Stars, so maybe she isn't looked at as the star of the team, but she has completely taken the reins and we are able to see her healthy, with that experience put together, coming off of Unrivaled where she was balling out. I have loved watching Shakira Austin this season.

quotes.speaker: Teresa Weatherspoon
quotes.summary_phrase: Teresa Weatherspoon on Shakira Austin's physical play and All-Star snub
quotes.excerpt: She's playing, she's playing, I think she kind of ticked off about that All-Star snub
quotes.quote: The only reason I didn't say her, because you are so right, she is really playing. And she's playing, she's playing, I think she kind of ticked off about that All-Star snub because she's been really, really playing incredible basketball. The only reason I didn't say because she was a starter. But when I tell you, I am enjoying watching her play. The energy that she plays with, and she's physical, and I love that part about her. She doesn't stop being physical. She's just playing really good basketball right now, and I think that's a great pick too.

quotes.speaker: Teresa Weatherspoon
quotes.summary_phrase: Teresa Weatherspoon on the defensive intensity required in the WNBA
quotes.excerpt: Individually you better be great. Individually you better be great defensively.
quotes.quote: Unrivaled has been great for those young women because it's really a breakdown to the five-on-five, and you all know this, everything is broken down in the threes anyway. And in this, individually you better be great. Individually you better be great defensively. You got to make sure you're guarding your yard, you're keeping that ball in front of you because there's too much space for these athletes. They are incredible in space.

quotes.speaker: Teresa Weatherspoon
quotes.summary_phrase: Teresa Weatherspoon on the coaching impact of Latricia Trammell
quotes.excerpt: She is something else. My, really something else.
quotes.quote: She is something else. My, really something else. Every day it was something funny. I'm about to laugh just thinking about it, the stuff she would say. She's crazy. She's crazy, shout out Latricia Trammell. She is thorough, thorough in her teaching, in her studying. Anything that I asked, the night before, and when we bring it back in to as coaches and coming together, the way that she brought it, you couldn't be happier as a coach to know that you have someone who brings things in that way every day. And then she does it with great laughter, joke behind joke behind joke. Oh, it's something.

quotes.speaker: Teresa Weatherspoon
quotes.summary_phrase: Teresa Weatherspoon on the breakout potential of Sydney Taylor
quotes.excerpt: That would be for me, Sydney Taylor. She has really gotten the eyes on her
quotes.quote: That would be for me, Sydney Taylor. She has really gotten the eyes on her once she's been allowed these minutes to showcase who she is. I think the one thing that really turned things for me with her is when I don't remember the team, but she missed a game-winning shot from the baseline, and Dwyane Wade was right there to console her. Her team came to console her, she was crying right there on the floor. That showed me that this kid really cares. Well, that opportunity came again for her against New York. She comes off and bang, she bangs it to let me know that she has some confidence.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Robinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jordan Robinson on Kayla McBride's record-breaking scoring performance
quotes.excerpt: Kayla McBride scored 43 points, 10 threes, set a WNBA record, 10 of them.
quotes.quote: This is somebody who we should be talking about. It should be on every headline, it should be leading every sports show, and that is Kayla McBride. Kayla McBride scored 43 points, 10 threes, set a WNBA record, 10 of them. You need two hands to count them. That's how many threes she scored. And still, I think because she's on the number one team in the Minnesota Lynx, and everyone is looking at Olivia Miles, as we should, but Nafisa Collier is back, Courtney Williams gets a lot of headlines, Natasha Howard is an All-Star, and somehow you still have this Kayla McBride who can go off for 43 on your roster and we're not talking about it enough.

quotes.speaker: Teresa Weatherspoon
quotes.summary_phrase: Teresa Weatherspoon on the importance of highlighting WNBA player achievements
quotes.excerpt: I'm tired of all the other headlines. Speak about our sport.
quotes.quote: I like how you spoke about that because I'm tired of all the other headlines. Speak about our sport. Speak about what our young women are doing and what they do between those four lines. This stuff is not easy. I think people think it's easy just step between the four lines and play. It's not. There's work behind this. Speak about what we do, speak about how they perform, speak about how many fans come to watch them to play. Speak about those great things that are happening and not all the other headlines.
